newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds rise but gains seen slowing.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds rise but gains seen slowing.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished higher Wednesday as the market benefitted more from news of corporate upgrades by Standard & Poor's but traders said the market's gains were set to slow in coming days.
"There was an important current of buyers on the upgrade news," said a trader at a foreign bank. "The market calmed down in the afternoon though."
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 was up 1/4 at 90-1/2, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 rose $0.20 to 125.90.

Another trader said the euphoria slowed down Wednesday afternoon because of a back-up in the yield on the U.S. 30-year treasury but also because the buying spree that set in Tuesday afternoon was partially motivated by lots of short positions in the market.
"The reality was that there were shorts in the market," said the trader.
He added that the market could now return to the same cautious mood of uncertainty on U.S. rates that plagued it for weeks before the upgrade news Tuesday.
Call money rates fell to 5.38 percent from 5.63 percent.
